verdict.root_cause: Every sampled PlaceOrder trace fails at the same point: checkoutservice's outbound client span to ShippingService/GetQuote returns ERROR in 0.4–2.6ms with no shippingservice server-side child span, while all prior calls (cartservice/Redis, productcatalogservice, currencyservice) succeed normally. That signature — fast, uniform, deterministic failure with the callee never producing a server span — means the call is being rejected at or before the shippingservice handler (connection refused / unavailable / immediate rejection), not that shipping is slow or that checkout has an internal bug. Checkout itself is healthy: it is alive, accepting requests and logging order starts through 09:14:28, but no order reaches payment, email or queue-write logging, exactly matching the trace evidence that execution aborts inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart. The simultaneous 09:12:45 alerts on accountingservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice, quoteservice and shippingservice are consistent with traffic starvation downstream of the stall rather than five independent faults — quoteservice sees no work because shipping never calls it, and the post-payment services see no work because checkout never gets that far. What made shippingservice stop serving was never established: no specialist was dispatched to shippingservice or quoteservice at all, and the only change query run covered checkoutservice alone (which showed no changes, correctly excluding a checkout-side deploy or flag flip). The mechanism is therefore an unavailable shipping dependency whose own failure mode — non-running artifact, wrong endpoint/port value, or its own downstream — remains unidentified.
verdict.reasoning: The trace evidence (tr_bb9484cf38ae) localizes the fault precisely and rules out every alternative hop in the checkout path: cart/Redis, productcatalog, currency all complete cleanly and are followed by later spans; payment, shipping-order and queue/email spans never appear because execution aborts at the quote step. The absence of a shippingservice server span under an erroring client span, combined with single-digit-millisecond durations, distinguishes rejection-at-the-callee from timeout or slowness, which is why dependency_latency does not fit. The log evidence (tr_d66c8ab1f361) independently corroborates the same shape from a different signal: order-start lines continue at steady cadence while all completion-stage lines vanish together, and no crash, restart or telemetry gap explains it. The change evidence (tr_188ed47f27e7) excludes a checkoutservice deploy, config push or flag flip in the onset window, which removes the most convenient bad_deploy/bad_config story on the alerting service itself and pushes causation to shippingservice — a service nobody queried. I decline to name bad_deploy or bad_config because both remain live and the evidence cannot separate them: a shipping pod that will not start and a shipping endpoint pointing at a wrong address produce the same fast-fail-with-no-server-span signature from checkout's vantage point, and the remediations (rollback vs config_revert) are different. The past cart incidents are a warning that the quiet, error-free service is often the broken one — here shippingservice emits nothing at all in checkout's logs — but they are pattern, not proof, and I have not treated their resolutions as this incident's. One inconsistency is unresolved and lowers confidence: the metric series (tr_8208b7da1b41) shows checkout error ratio peaking near 0.30 with zero-error points, while traces show 100% of sampled PlaceOrder calls failing; this is probably a window/sampling artifact (metrics span 08:59:30–09:14:30 including pre-onset minutes, and checkout serves non-PlaceOrder RPCs) but it was never reconciled.
open_questions: Nothing at all was queried on shippingservice — no logs, metrics, traces or change history. Whether its pods are running, crash-looping, failing readiness, or rejecting connections is entirely unestablished.

Was there a deploy, image change, config edit or flag flip on shippingservice (or quoteservice) near 09:09? The only change query covered checkoutservice and only 08:59:30–09:14:30; the 08:30–08:59 span and all dependencies are unqueried.

Is shippingservice itself failing, or failing because quoteservice (which also alerted at 09:12:45) is unavailable to it? Without a shipping-side trace or log we cannot tell whether quoteservice is a starved victim or the origin.

Why does checkout's error ratio peak at ~0.30 with zero-error intervals when every sampled PlaceOrder trace is ERROR? Unreconciled — could be pre-onset data in the window, non-PlaceOrder RPC traffic diluting the ratio, or trace sampling bias toward the failing period.
The log window 09:01:04–09:11:05 was truncated and never observed; error/warning lines naming the failing dependency could exist there and would change the picture.
Whether the correct fix is rollback, config_revert or restart depends entirely on shippingservice's state, which is why no remediation is named here.

The five 09:12:45 alerts are interpreted as traffic starvation downstream of the stall; this is inference from topology and the log/trace pattern, not confirmed by any per-service check of accountingservice, emailservice or frauddetectionservice.
